convention: The hand-verified edges of this program (hand-verified-edges.json) that the readers do not draw, each with the reason found by reading why. tests/integration/live-docs/oracle.test.ts fails on a missing edge this ledger does not list, and on a listed edge that is drawn again or no longer asserted. Paths are relative to this file.

misses.cause: The designer file declares one field per server control and names nothing else. The page publishes those controls' IDs as symbols (serverForm, PaymentsEnabledHidden, GatewayBaseUrlHidden), but the C# reader reads a field's declaration as the file's own symbol, never as a use of the page's control of the same ID, and the designer file holds no directive or name of its page to link by.

The endpoint name is built at run time: ServiceRouting.EndpointNameFor(workload, environment) joins the constant EndpointPrefix to two parameters. The C# reader folds only constant strings, so it knows no name for the ChannelFactory<IPaymentService> to match against App.config's client endpoints, and matching their shared prefix PaymentService. would be a guess.

The class's only ties to the procedure are a doc comment, which no reader reads, and its property names, which are the procedure's result columns: the SQL reader publishes no result column. The call that binds the class to the procedure's result, Database.SqlQuery<PostPaymentRow> with dbo.usp_PostPayment, is in PaymentsContext.cs, whose own edge to the script is drawn.
